questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu aha e ji akpọ ihe ọmụmụ gbasara ụda okwu na otu e si amata ha n'akụkụ ọnụ mmadụ?
questions.explanation: Phonetics is the branch of language study concerned with the physical production and articulation of speech sounds.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Mgbochiume 'gb' na 'kp' bụ ụdị mgbochiume dị aṅaa n'asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: 'gb' and 'kp' are co-articulated (labial-velar) consonants written as digraphs in the Onwu orthography.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ụdaume Igbo abụọ dị iche na ha na-adịghị adịkọta n'otu okwu n'ihi ndakọrịta ụdaume bụ
options: Ụdaume mkpuchi (a, e, i, o, u) na ụdaume mkpughe (ị, ọ, ụ)
questions.explanation: Igbo's eight vowels split into two harmony sets often described loosely as the a/e/i/o/u set and ị/ọ/ụ set; words generally draw vowels from only one set.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Olu (tone) n'asụsụ Igbo nwere ike ịrụ ọrụ dị aṅaa n'okwu?
options: Ịgbanwe nzube okwu, dịka 'akwụ' (nut) na 'akwụ' (palm tree) mgbe olu ha dị iche
Ọ na-arụ ọrụ dị ka akara ntụgharị naanị
Ọ dịghị mkpa ma ọlị n'ịkọwa okwu
questions.explanation: Tone is phonemic in Igbo: two words with identical spelling but different tone patterns can have completely different meanings.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị ụda a na-akpọ ụda ntụle (nasal sound) n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Ụda a na-esite n'imi apụta dịka 'm', 'n', na 'ṅ'
questions.explanation: Nasal sounds such as m, n, and ṅ are produced with airflow passing through the nose.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Mkpụrụedemede 'ṅ' n'asụsụ Igbo na-egosipụta ụda dị aṅaa?
options: Ụda ntụle azụ akpịrị (velar nasal), dịka na 'aṅaa'
questions.explanation: 'ṅ' represents the velar nasal sound, similar to the 'ng' sound at the end of the English word 'sing'.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ikpe olu, olu ndabere (downstep) na-apụta mgbe
options: olu ala abụọ na-esote ibe ha
olu elu si n'olu elu ọzọ pụta ma dịnyere ala ntakịrị karịa olu elu mbụ
questions.explanation: Downstep occurs when a high tone follows another high tone but is realised slightly lower than the preceding one.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọnọdụ mgbe otu ụdaume na-efunahụ n'okwu abụọ jikọrọ ọnụ iji mee ka ha kwụọ ọtọ nke ọma (elision)?
questions.explanation: Vowel elision is the dropping of a vowel sound, often at a word boundary, to make speech flow more smoothly, e.g. 'a na-eri' becoming 'a na-eri' contracted forms in fast speech.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu njirimara a na-akọwa mgbochiume 'gh' na 'kw' n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Ha bụ mgbochiume e ji abụọ edepụta otu ụda (digraphs)
questions.explanation: 'gh' and 'kw' are digraphs — two letters combined to represent a single consonant sound in Igbo orthography.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mpaghara ike a na-adabere na ya mgbe a na-akpọpụta okwu, dịka isi mkpụrụedemede na-anata olu elu?
questions.explanation: Stress or prominence refers to the relative emphasis given to certain syllables during pronunciation.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'usoro ndakọrịta ụdaume, mgbe otu okwu ji ụdaume site n'otu ụdị (set), okwu ahụ na-egosi
options: Ọdịnaya na nhazi ụda kwekọrọ n'ime otu okwu
questions.explanation: Vowel harmony ensures internal phonological consistency, with all vowels in a word drawn from the same harmonic set.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Usoro mkpụrụedemede e ji ede Igbo ugbu a bụ
questions.explanation: The Onwu orthography, adopted in 1961 by the Onwu Committee, remains the officially recognised standard for writing Igbo today.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu okwu bụ nkeji akwụkwọ (loan word) e siri na Bekee bata n'asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: 'Motọ' (motor/vehicle) is an English loan word adapted into Igbo, unlike the other listed words which are native Igbo terms.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu njirimara a na-akpọ okwu abụọ e jikọtara ọnụ imepụta otu echiche ọhụrụ, dịka 'aka' + 'ọrụ' = 'akaọrụ'?
questions.explanation: Compounding joins two independent words to create a new word with a combined or extended meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'asụsụ Igbo, okwu 'nwaanyị' pụtara
questions.explanation: 'Nwaanyị' is the standard Igbo word for a female/woman, derived historically from 'nwa' (child) plus a female-marking element.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mkpụrụokwu bụ nkịtị (antonym) nke okwu 'ọma'?
questions.explanation: 'Ọjọọ' (bad) is the direct opposite of 'ọma' (good) in Igbo.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu okwu kwekọrọ n'ọdịdị nzube (synonym) na 'ịnyịnya'?
questions.explanation: 'Enyi-egbu ije' is a descriptive alternate term sometimes used for horse-like fast-moving animals; among the options it is the closest paired reference, while ewu (goat), aturu (sheep) and nkịta (dog) are unrelated animals.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ okwu e mepụtara ọhụrụ iji kwado echiche igbe ozi n'ọgbara ọhụrụ, dịka 'igwe okwu' maka telivishọn?
questions.explanation: Coinage is the invention of new words, often to name new concepts or technologies not previously captured in the language.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọnụọgụgụ mkpụrụedemede dị n'agbụrụ mkpụrụedemede Onwu e ji ede Igbo?
questions.explanation: The Onwu orthography's alphabet consists of 36 letters, including digraphs such as gb, gh, kp, nw, ny, and gw.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Okwu 'igbe ozi' n'asụsụ Igbo ọhụrụ na-egosipụta ihe a na-akpọ na Bekee
questions.explanation: 'Igbe ozi' (literally 'message box') is a coined Igbo term used to describe a communication device such as a radio.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ndabere (register) okwu 'nna ochie' na-egosi n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Nna nna, ma ọ bụ nna nke agadi
questions.explanation: 'Nna ochie' refers to one's grandfather (father's father) or an elderly paternal figure in the extended family register.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ọ bụ olee mkpụrụokwu ka a na-eji akọwa 'onye nkuzi' n'akwụkwọ Igbo ọgbara ọhụrụ?
questions.explanation: 'Onye nkuzi' is the standard modern Igbo term for a teacher, from 'kuzi' (to teach).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu njirimara nzube nke okwu 'ọgụ' n'ọdịdị dị iche iche dabere n'olu ya?
options: Ọ pụtara 'ntagbu' (war/fight) ma ọ bụ 'ọtụtụ' (broom) dabere n'olu
questions.explanation: Depending on its tone, 'ọgụ' can mean 'war/fight' or 'broom', illustrating the importance of tone in distinguishing lexical meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'Nnukwu nwoke ahụ na-arị ugbo', 'nnukwu' bụ ụdị okwu dị aṅaa?
questions.explanation: 'Nnukwu' (big/great) modifies the noun 'nwoke' (man), making it an adjective.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'Ọ na-agba ọsọ ọsọ', 'ọsọ ọsọ' bụ ụdị okwu dị aṅaa?
questions.explanation: 'Ọsọ ọsọ' (quickly, hurriedly) modifies the verb 'agba' (to run), functioning as an adverb of manner.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ngwaa kwesịrị ekwesị mejupụta ohere efu: 'Anyị ___ ga-aga ahịa echi.'
questions.explanation: The future tense marker 'ga-' correctly attaches to the auxiliary verb structure preceding the main verb 'aga' in this sentence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọnọdụ ozugbo (present continuous) dabara adaba n'ahịrịokwu: '___ na-eri nri ugbu a.'
questions.explanation: 'Ọ na-eri nri ugbu a' (He/she is eating now) uses the pronoun 'Ọ' with the continuous aspect marker 'na-' already on the verb.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ụtọasụsụ Igbo, ihe a na-akpọ 'nnochi aha onwe' (reflexive pronoun) bụ
options: Onwe m, onwe gị, onwe ya
Nke m, nke gị, nke ya
questions.explanation: Reflexive pronouns like 'onwe m' (myself), 'onwe gị' (yourself), and 'onwe ya' (himself/herself) refer the action back to the subject.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ahịrịokwu ndabere na-egosi ọnọdụ gara aga zuru oke (simple past)?
questions.explanation: 'Ọ gara ahịa ụnyaahụ' (He/she went to the market yesterday) expresses a completed past action, marked by the past tense form 'gara'.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'Ada na Chika bịara', 'Ada na Chika' bụ
questions.explanation: 'Ada na Chika' is the compound subject performing the action of coming ('bịara').

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị njikọ okwu bụ 'ma ọ bụ na' n'ahịrịokwu Igbo?
options: Njikọ okwu na-egosi nhọrọ ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ (conditional/alternative)
questions.explanation: 'Ma ọ bụ na' functions as a conditional/alternative conjunction, roughly meaning 'if' or 'or if' depending on context.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ nnochi aha 'ọ' na-arụ n'ahịrịokwu: 'Ọ bịara ụlọ m.'?
options: Ọ na-anọchi anya ihe a na-eme (object pronoun)
Ọ na-anọchi anya onye na-eme ihe (subject pronoun)
questions.explanation: 'Ọ' functions as a third-person singular subject pronoun (he/she/it) performing the action of coming.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị ahịrịokwu bụ nke a: 'Ọ bụ eziokwu na Chika na-agụ akwụkwọ?'
questions.explanation: This sentence asks a question, making it an interrogative sentence, marked by 'Ọ bụ eziokwu na...' as a question frame.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mgbakwunye (affix) dị n'okwu 'nna-anyị' na-egosi?
questions.explanation: '-anyị' attached to 'nna' indicates possession, forming 'our father'.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ahịrịokwu 'Nwatakịrị ahụ nwụrụ anwụ n'ihi ọrịa', 'n'ihi ọrịa' bụ
options: Ngwa mbuuzo na-egosi ihe kpatara ihe (cause)
questions.explanation: 'N'ihi ọrịa' (because of illness) is a prepositional phrase indicating the cause of the child's death.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Mgbe a na-agụ otu akụkọ maka aghọtaazaa, ihe kacha mkpa bụ
options: Ịghọta isi ozi na nkọwa dị n'akụkọ ahụ
Ịgụ ngwa ngwa karịa ndị ọzọ
questions.explanation: The main goal of a comprehension exercise is understanding the core message and supporting details of the passage.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Edemede na-akọwa echiche onye edemede site n'iji ihe akaebe kwado ya ka a na-akpọ
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay presents and defends a position using supporting evidence and reasoning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Akwụkwọ ozi ekpo ọkụ (formal letter) n'asụsụ Igbo na-amalitekarị site na
options: Aha na adreesị onye na-edeghachi na onye a na-edegara akwụkwọ ozi ahụ
questions.explanation: A formal Igbo letter typically opens with the sender's address, date, recipient's address/title, and a formal salutation.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Nchịkọta (summary) nke otu edemede kwesịrị ịbụ
options: Nkenke nke na-egosipụta naanị isi ihe dị mkpa n'edemede ahụ
Ederede zuru ezu nke edemede ahụ n'uju
questions.explanation: A summary distills the essential main points of a text into a concise version, omitting minor details.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'ide edemede akụkọ (narrative essay), ihe dị mkpa bụ
options: Nhazi ihe omume n'usoro oge (chronological order)
questions.explanation: A narrative essay generally organises events in the order they occurred, following a clear beginning, middle, and end.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Mgbe a na-agụ ajụjụ aghọtaazaa nke sitere n'otu akụkọ, ọ bụ ezi omume ka
options: A gụọ akụkọ ahụ tupu a lebara ajụjụ anya
A lelịa akụkọ ahụ anya kpamkpam
A zaa ajụjụ tupu a gụọ akụkọ ahụ
A jụ ihe niile metụtara akụkọ ahụ
questions.explanation: Best practice is to read the passage carefully first to build understanding before attempting to answer the questions.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Edemede na-akọwapụta ọnọdụ, mmadụ, ma ọ bụ ebe n'ụzọ zuru ezu ka a na-akpọ
questions.explanation: A descriptive essay vividly portrays a person, place, or situation using rich sensory detail.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nkà a na-achọ n'aka onye na-ede edemede zuru oke n'asụsụ Igbo?
options: Nhazi echiche doro anya na iji ụtọasụsụ ziri ezi
Ide n'enweghị isi ihe doro anya
questions.explanation: Strong Igbo essay writing requires clear, logical organisation of ideas alongside correct grammar and paragraphing.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'akwụkwọ ozi enyi na enyi (informal letter), ndabere okwu a na-ejikarị bụ
options: Okwu efe efe, nke enyi na ezinụlọ na-eji
questions.explanation: Informal letters use a relaxed, familiar register appropriate for friends and family, unlike the formal register of official correspondence.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ihe kpatara e ji akụziri ụmụ akwụkwọ otu e si ede edemede n'usoro bụ
options: Ka ha nwee ike izikọrịta echiche ha n'ụzọ doro anya
Ka ha ghara ịgụ akwụkwọ ọzọ
questions.explanation: Teaching structured essay writing equips students to communicate their ideas clearly and effectively.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Agụmagụ Ọnụ (oral literature) bụ
options: Agụmagụ e si n'ọnụ na-agbasa n'ọgbọ ruo n'ọgbọ, n'edeghị ede ede
questions.explanation: Oral literature is passed down verbally through generations without being originally recorded in writing.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ilu (proverbs) n'omenala Igbo bụ
options: Nkenke okwu amamihe ndị okenye na-eji akọwa echiche miri emi
questions.explanation: Proverbs (ilu) are concise, traditional sayings loaded with wisdom, commonly used especially by elders to convey deep meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ilu Igbo bụ 'Ọkụkọ mara mma amaghị na ọ bụ nri' na-egosi echiche bụ
options: Ọ bụ maka ọrụ ugbo naanị
Mma anya adịghị egosi ọnọdụ ihe n'ime
Ọ bụ maka ịkụ egwu naanị
Ọkụkọ dị mma karịa anụ ọzọ
questions.explanation: This proverb ('A beautiful fowl does not know it is meant for the pot') warns that outward beauty can hide underlying danger or fate.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ilu 'Onye kwuo eziokwu, ọ dịghị mkpa ka o cheta ihe o kwuru' na-akọwa isi echiche
options: Ị ga-echeta okwu ụgha mgbe niile
Eziokwu na-adịgide, nghọtahie adịghị adị n'ịkọ ya
questions.explanation: This proverb ('He who speaks the truth need not remember what he said') teaches that truth is consistent and needs no memorised cover-up, unlike lies.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ akụkọ ọdịnala nke na-akọwa mmalite ụwa ma ọ bụ ihe omimi banyere chi?
questions.explanation: Myths (nkọmịrịkọ) explain cosmic origins or the actions of deities and supernatural beings within Igbo oral tradition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Akụkọ ifo (folktale) n'omenala Igbo na-ejikarị
options: Naanị mmadụ dị ndụ mere ka ha bụrụ ndị isi n'akụkọ
Anụmanụ dị iche iche mere ka ha bụrụ ndị isi n'akụkọ (dịka mbe na agụ)
questions.explanation: Igbo folktales commonly feature anthropomorphised animal characters, with the tortoise (mbe) being one of the most famous trickster figures.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'akụkọ ifo Igbo, mbe (tortoise) na-ejikarị anọ dịka onye
options: Onye nwere ume karịa ha niile
questions.explanation: The tortoise is the archetypal trickster in Igbo folktales, often using cunning and cleverness to outwit larger, stronger animals.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Agwụgwa (riddle) na-eji ọkịkọ ya bụ
options: Ịnwale amamihe na uche ọsọ ọsọ nke onye na-aza ya
questions.explanation: Riddles are a traditional oral game designed to test wit, quick thinking, and cleverness.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Mbem (chant/incantation) n'omenala Igbo na-ejikarị apụta n'oge
options: Emume ọdịnala dịka akwamozu ma ọ bụ mgbamume
questions.explanation: Chants are rhythmic oral performances typically recited during ceremonies such as funerals, festivals, or masquerade displays.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ ndị isi ilu na-arụ n'okwu ekwe ekwe (rhetoric) ndị Igbo?
options: Ha na-eme ka okwu ghara ịpụta ìhè
Ha na-eme ka okwu dị mma, dị ike, na dị ime omimi
questions.explanation: Proverbs enrich Igbo rhetoric, giving speech elegance, persuasive power, and layered meaning — hence the saying 'Ilu bụ mmanụ e ji eri okwu' (proverbs are the palm oil with which words are eaten).

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ilu 'Aka nri kwọọ aka ekpe, aka ekpe akwọọ aka nri' na-akọwa isi echiche
options: Mkpa mmekọrịta na inyeaka onwe onye n'echiche onye ọzọ (mutual cooperation)
questions.explanation: This proverb ('the right hand washes the left, and the left washes the right') emphasises the importance of mutual assistance and cooperation.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ egwu ọdịnala nke a na-abụkarị iji kwanyere agadi nna ma ọ bụ nne ùgwù n'akwamozu?
questions.explanation: Dirges (abụ akwamozu) are traditional funeral songs performed to honour the deceased and comfort mourners.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ọ bụ olee otu akụkọ ifo si adịkarị na njedebe ya?
options: Ọ na-enwekarị mmụta ma ọ bụ ihe onye na-ege ntị ga-amụta
Ọ dịghị mgbe ọ na-enwe njedebe
questions.explanation: Igbo folktales often conclude with a moral lesson meant to instruct the listener, typically children.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Nkata/akụkọ gbasara 'Ekwensu' n'echiche ọdịnala Igbo na-egosipụta ya dịka
options: Mmụọ ọjọọ ma ọ bụ onye na-arụ ọrụ nrụgide n'echiche ọdịnala
questions.explanation: In traditional Igbo cosmology, Ekwensu is often associated with a malevolent or mischievous spirit figure, distinct from destiny-related deities like Chi.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu onye edemede a maara nke ọma maka akwụkwọ akụkọ Igbo 'Omenụko'?
questions.explanation: 'Omenụko' is a foundational Igbo-language novel written by Leopold Bell-Gam, among the early published works of written Igbo literature.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Akwụkwọ akụkọ 'Ije Odumodu Jere' bụ ọrụ onye edemede
questions.explanation: 'Ije Odumodu Jere' is a well-known early Igbo-language novel written by D. N. Achara.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Agụmagụ edere ede (written literature) dị iche na agụmagụ ọnụ n'ihi na
options: A na-edekpu ya n'akwụkwọ ma nwee onye edemede a maara aha ya
A naghị adekọ ya ma ọlị
questions.explanation: Unlike anonymous, orally transmitted literature, written literature is recorded in text and typically attributed to a known author.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ụdị agụmagụ e ji akpọ ihe odide dị ka egwuregwu ejije (drama) na abụ (poetry) tinyere akụkọ (prose)?
options: Ụdị agụmagụ atọ bụ isi (major literary genres)
Ọ bụ mmemme mbọsị ụbọchị naanị
questions.explanation: Prose, drama, and poetry are widely recognised as the three major genres within written literature, including Igbo literature.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Onye edemede a maara nke ọma maka mkpụrụ akwụkwọ akụkọ Bekee metụtara ndụ Igbo bụ 'Things Fall Apart' bụ
questions.explanation: Though written in English, 'Things Fall Apart' by Chinua Achebe draws deeply on Igbo culture and is a landmark reference point often studied alongside Igbo-language literature.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Onye edemede a maara nke ọma maka ọtụtụ akwụkwọ akụkọ Igbo dịka 'Ukwa Ruo Oge Ya Ọ Daa' bụ
questions.explanation: Tony Uchenna Ubesie was a prolific and influential Igbo-language novelist known for works including 'Ukwa Ruo Oge Ya Ọ Daa'.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: N'egwuregwu ejije (drama) e dere n'asụsụ Igbo, akụkụ dị mkpa bụ
options: Okwu ndị agbatakwụkwọ na-ekwu n'ihu ndị na-ekiri (dialogue and performance)
questions.explanation: Drama centres on dialogue delivered by characters and performed before an audience, distinguishing it from prose and poetry.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Abụ (poetry) e dere n'asụsụ Igbo na-ejikarị
options: Okwu a họpụtara nke ọma, nwere ụda na ọkpụkpọ akụkụ (rhythm and imagery)
questions.explanation: Igbo poetry, like poetry generally, relies on carefully chosen language, rhythm, and vivid imagery to convey meaning.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ọ bụ olee ọrụ isi nke onye edemede agụmagụ edere ede na-arụ n'ọdịnala Igbo ọgbara ọhụrụ?
options: Idekọ ọdịnala na echiche ọha n'ụzọ ga-adịgide adịgide
questions.explanation: Modern Igbo writers often use written literature to preserve and transmit cultural values and traditions for lasting record.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ọrụ agụmagụ Igbo ọgbara ọhụrụ na-arụ n'agbata mba dị iche iche?
options: Igosipụta ọdịnala na echiche ndị Igbo n'ihu ụwa
questions.explanation: Contemporary Igbo literature, whether written directly in Igbo or drawing on Igbo culture, helps showcase Igbo heritage to a wider, international audience.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ echiche ọdịnala Igbo banyere onyinye onye ọ bụla si n'aka Chukwu tupu a mụọ ya, nke na-eduzi akara aka ya?
questions.explanation: In Igbo cosmology, Chi is one's personal spiritual guardian or destiny-force, believed to be assigned by Chukwu before birth.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ọfọ n'omenala Igbo bụ
options: Akụ na-egosi ikike na eziokwu, nke ndị okenye na ndị ndú na-ejide
questions.explanation: The ofo staff symbolises authority, justice, and truth, traditionally held by elders and lineage heads as a mark of legitimate power.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Nzuzo nke Ekpe ma ọ bụ Mmanwu n'omenala Igbo bụ
options: Otu ọdịnala nwoke, nke jikọtara na mmụọ ndị nwụrụ anwụ na ọdịnala obodo
questions.explanation: The masquerade (mmanwu) institution is a traditional men's society associated with ancestral spirits and important in community governance and ceremony.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Iru mmụọ/Igba afa n'omenala Igbo bụ omenala metụtara
options: Ịjụta ase dibia afa maka nsogbu ma ọ bụ ihe izizi
questions.explanation: Consulting a diviner (dibia afa) is a traditional practice of seeking spiritual insight into problems, causes of misfortune, or the future.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Iwa akwa (age-grade/title institution) dị iche na 'Ọzọ' n'ihi na Ọzọ bụ
options: Otu nzere ùgwù kachasị elu nwoke ọ bụla nwere ike ịnata n'ọha
questions.explanation: The Ọzọ title is among the highest traditional honours a man can attain in many Igbo communities, distinct from age-grade groupings.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Igba ndụ (covenant/oath-taking) n'omenala Igbo na-ejikarị
options: Ana ma ọ bụ chi dịka onyeàma n'ọgbụgba ndụ
questions.explanation: Traditional oath-taking often invokes the earth deity (ana) or a chi/deity as witness, binding participants to the covenant.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ọha na eze n'ọtụtụ obodo Igbo bụ usoro ọchịchị dabere na
options: Nzukọ ndị okenye na ọha mmadụ iji were mkpebi (republican/communal governance)
Otu eze zuru ike ijide ọchịchị naanị
questions.explanation: Traditional Igbo governance in many communities was historically decentralised and republican, based on councils of elders and communal decision-making rather than a single centralised monarch.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Emume Ịwa Ji (New Yam Festival) n'omenala Igbo na-egosipụta
options: Ekele a na-enye Ana na chi maka owuwe ihe ubi ji ọhụrụ
Ememme ọlụlụ di na nwunye naanị
questions.explanation: The New Yam Festival is a major traditional harvest celebration expressing thanksgiving to the earth deity and gods for a successful yam harvest.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ikenga n'omenala Igbo bụ ihe oyiyi na-egosipụta
options: Ike aka nwoke na ihe ọ na-arụpụta (personal achievement and strength)
questions.explanation: Ikenga is a traditional symbolic carving representing personal power, strength of will, and achievement, often owned by men.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ndị nze na ọzọ n'obodo Igbo na-arụkarị ọrụ
options: Ndụmọdụ na nchekwa iwu na ọdịnala obodo
questions.explanation: Titled elders (nze na ọzọ) traditionally serve as custodians of custom, offering counsel and upholding community law and tradition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu steeti a na-akpọ 'Ala Igbo' bụ isi na Naịjirịa ugbu a?
options: Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, na Imo (na akụkụ Delta na Rivers)
questions.explanation: The core Igbo-speaking states in Nigeria today are commonly identified as Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo, with Igbo communities also in parts of Delta and Rivers.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ọtụtụ mmadụ na-asụ Igbo dịka asụsụ mbụ ha n'ụwa taa fọrọ nke nta ka ọ bụrụ
options: Ihe ka mmadụ nde iri atọ (over 30 million)
questions.explanation: Igbo is one of Nigeria's major languages, spoken as a first language by tens of millions of people worldwide, commonly estimated at over 30 million.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Ụbọchị Mmemme Ndị Igbo n'ụwa (World Igbo Day) na-abụkarị mgbe ọ bụla
questions.explanation: World Igbo Day/Igbo Cultural Festival celebrations are commonly observed in September, celebrating Igbo heritage and identity globally.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu otu ọdịnala mmekọrịta na azụmahịa ndị Igbo maara nke ọma n'akụkụ Naịjirịa na mba ndị ọzọ?
options: Igba boyi/azụmahịa mba ofesi (apprenticeship and trading system)
questions.explanation: The Igbo trade apprenticeship system (igba boyi/igba odibo) is a widely recognised traditional entrepreneurial model still practised and studied today.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu asụsụ e ji akpọ Naịjirịa n'asụsụ Igbo?
questions.explanation: 'Naịjirịa' is the standard Igbo rendering of the country name Nigeria.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Gọọmentị etiti Naịjirịa na-akwadokarị mmụta Igbo n'ụlọ akwụkwọ dabere n'usoro
options: Iwu banyere azụmahịa mba ofesi naanị
Iwu ọgbọ mmụta mba (National Policy on Education), nke na-akwado mmụta asụsụ obodo
questions.explanation: Nigeria's National Policy on Education promotes the teaching of major indigenous languages, including Igbo, in schools.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu nsogbu a na-ekwukarị banyere ọdịnihu asụsụ Igbo n'oge a?
options: Ọ nwere ike ọ ga-akpụ ọtụtụ mba ọzọ
Ọ bụghị asụsụ e ji ede akwụkwọ
Ntakasị ọnụọgụgụ ụmụaka na-asụ ya n'ụlọ (declining intergenerational transmission)
questions.explanation: A widely discussed concern among linguists and cultural advocates is the declining rate at which Igbo is being passed down to children at home.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu otu nzukọ mba ụwa a maara nke ọma nke na-eweta olileanya maka nchekwa asụsụ Igbo n'ụlọ akwụkwọ na teknụzụ?
options: Ọ dịghị mmepụta ọ bụla e mere
Naanị ndị mba ofesi kwadoro ya
Mmadụ na-emepụta ngwa mgbako (apps) na akara ngosi (software) iji kụziri Igbo
questions.explanation: Language-technology efforts, such as mobile apps, digital dictionaries, and machine-translation projects, have grown in recent years to support Igbo language preservation.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmemme na-eme kwa afọ n'ọtụtụ obodo Igbo iji mee ememme ọ bụla otu mba (dịka mmụba obodo)?
questions.explanation: Many Igbo towns hold annual cultural festivals celebrating heritage, homecoming, and communal identity.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mkpa ọ bara ka ndị Igbo na-eme mgbalị ka ụmụaka mụta ịsụ Igbo n'ụlọ n'oge a?
options: Ka ha ghara ịmụ asụsụ Bekee ma ọlị
Ka asụsụ na ọdịnala Igbo ghara ikpochapụ n'ọgbọ na-abịa
questions.explanation: Efforts to raise children speaking Igbo at home are widely encouraged to safeguard the language and culture for future generations.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mkpụrụokwu ndị na-egosi ọnụọgụgụ n'asụsụ Igbo, dịka 'otu', 'abụọ', 'atọ'?
questions.explanation: Numerals such as 'otu' (one), 'abụọ' (two), and 'atọ' (three) are the Igbo words for counting numbers.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu aha a na-akpọ nwoke bụ di n'ezinụlọ Igbo?
questions.explanation: 'Di' is the Igbo word for husband, the male head of a household in a family unit.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ọrụ ubi bụ isi ọrụ ndị Igbo ka ọtụtụ n'ime ha na-arụ?
questions.explanation: Farming (ọrụ ugbo) has traditionally been a central economic activity among the Igbo people.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ala ndị Igbo bi na ya, dị na mba Naijiria?
questions.explanation: Igboland (Ala Igbo) refers to the geographical and cultural homeland of the Igbo people in southeastern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nzụkọ obodo a na-eme kwa afọ iji chekwaa omenala na ịkpọghachite ndị obodo?
options: Ememme obodo/nzukọ ala (annual town reunion/cultural festival)
questions.explanation: Annual town reunions and cultural festivals are common among Igbo communities to preserve heritage and reconnect indigenes.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu okwu Igbo maka 'ezi na ụlọ', ya bụ ndị mmadụ jikọtara ọnụ site n'ọmụmụ?
questions.explanation: 'Ezinụlọ' is the Igbo word for family, the basic unit of kinship and social organisation.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ nzuko ndị okenye n'obodo Igbo na-ekpebi ihe ndị metụtara obodo?
questions.explanation: A council of elders (amala or ndị okenye) traditionally plays a key decision-making role in Igbo communal governance.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu mgbe a na-eji akwụkwọ akara ejiji dị ka nsibidi mara maka ya n'ime ọdịnala Igbo?
options: Ọ bụghị ihe ọ bụla metụtara ọdịnala Igbo
Naanị maka mgbasa ozi ọgbara ọhụrụ
Iji dị ka ụdị ederede/akara ozi ọdịnala (a traditional ideographic writing/symbol system)
questions.explanation: Nsibidi is a traditional system of symbols/ideographs historically used in parts of Igbo and neighbouring cultures for communication.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ ndụ mmụọ na okwukwe ndị Igbo kwenyere na ya tupu mbata ndị ndị ọzọ?
questions.explanation: 'Odinani' refers to the traditional Igbo religious and cultural belief system that predates the arrival of other religions.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu ihe a na-akpọ mmemme a na-eme mgbe a mụrụ nwa ọhụrụ n'ime ndị Igbo iji gosi obi ụtọ?
options: Ememme ọlụlụ di na nwunye kaanị
questions.explanation: A naming ceremony is held to celebrate and formally name a newborn child within Igbo tradition.

questions.subject: Igbo
questions.text: Kedu okwu Igbo maka nwoke na-elekọta obodo dịka onye isi ala n'ọdịnala?
questions.explanation: 'Igwe' or 'Eze' is the title commonly used for a traditional ruler in many Igbo communities.
